results.name: Cross Body Shoulder Stretch
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder width apart and your arms relaxed by your sides.
Raise one arm straight across the front of your chest at shoulder height.
Grasp your upper arm just above the elbow with your opposite hand and gently pull it closer to your chest while keeping your shoulders relaxed.
Hold the stretch, then slowly release and repeat on the opposite side.
tips: Pull from your upper arm rather than your forearm or wrist.
Keep your shoulders level and avoid shrugging them toward your ears.
Stretch only until you feel a comfortable pull in the back of your shoulder.
Inhale before applying the stretch and exhale as you gently pull your arm closer.
results.description: Cross Body Shoulder Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Rotator Cuff.

results.name: Crossover Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch
instructions: Begin in a lunge position with your right foot on the floor and your left knee on the floor, ensuring both legs are bent at 90 degrees.
Engage your core and rotate your torso towards your right leg, placing both arms straight and pulling on the outside of your right thigh.
Gently push your hips forward while keeping your back straight to stretch.
Hold this position for the desired duration, then switch sides and repeat.
tips: Ensure your front knee is aligned over your ankle to avoid unnecessary strain on your knee joint.
Perform the stretch with control to avoid overextending your hip flexors.
Breathe deeply and steadily throughout the stretch, inhaling through your nose and exhaling through your mouth.
results.description: Crossover Kneeling Hip Flexor Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Hamstrings.

results.name: Crouching Heel Back Calf Stretch
instructions: Begin standing with your legs wide in a semi-lunge position, turned to the right side, with your left leg extended back and your right knee bent.
Bend forward at the hips and place your hands on the floor in front of you for balance, keeping your back as straight as possible.
Push your left heel down towards the floor, feeling a stretch in your left calf muscle.
Hold the stretch for the desired duration, then switch sides and repeat the stretch on the right side.
tips: Focus on keeping your back straight and your shoulders down and away from your ears.
Perform the stretch with control to avoid overextending your calf muscles.
Breathe deeply and steadily throughout the stretch, inhaling through your nose and exhaling through your mouth.
Ensure your supporting leg (the one in front) remains bent to maintain balance.
results.description: Crouching Heel Back Calf Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps, Hamstrings, Glutes.

results.name: Dead Hang Stretch
instructions: Begin by standing under a pull-up bar or a similar overhead bar.
Reach up and grasp the bar with both hands, palms facing forward (overhand grip), and your hands shoulder-width apart.
Allow your body to hang freely with your feet off the floor, keeping your arms fully extended and your shoulders relaxed.
Hold this position for the desired duration, focusing on deep breathing and maintaining a relaxed grip.
tips: Keep your shoulders relaxed and avoid shrugging them towards your ears.
Focus on deep, steady breaths to enhance the stretch and promote relaxation.
Use a bar that is high enough to allow your body to hang freely without touching the floor.
If you find it challenging to maintain the grip, use chalk to prevent slipping.
Ensure the bar and your grip are secure to avoid any accidents during the stretch.
results.description: Dead Hang Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Forearms, Chest.

results.name: Dumbbell RDL Stretch Isometric
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in your left hand, arm fully extended by your side, and your palm facing your thigh.
Hinge at your hips, lowering the dumbbell towards the floor while raising your left leg straight behind you, keeping it in line with your body. Your left leg should move in unison with your torso.
Continue lowering the dumbbell until your torso is parallel to the floor and you feel a stretch in your hamstrings.
Hold this stretched position for the desired duration, then return to the starting position.
tips: Focus on hinging at your hips rather than bending your back.
Keep your shoulders retracted and your chest lifted throughout the movement.
Ensure your standing foot remains flat on the floor, with your weight distributed evenly.
results.description: Dumbbell RDL Stretch Isometric is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back.

results.name: Dynamic Back Stretch
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms straight down by your sides.
Explosively swing your arms upwards in a wide arc until they are overhead, stretching your back muscles dynamically.
Immediately swing your arms back down to your sides in a controlled manner, allowing your back to relax.
Repeat the movement continuously for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your movements fluid and controlled to maximize the stretch and avoid any sudden jerks that could cause injury.
Engage your core muscles to support your lower back throughout the movement.
Ensure your knees are slightly bent to maintain balance and reduce strain on your lower back.
results.description: Dynamic Back Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

results.name: Elbow Back Stretch
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms at your sides.
Bring both hands behind you and place them on your lower back, fingers pointing downward.
Gently push your hips forward and lean your upper body backward, feeling a stretch in your chest and shoulders.
Hold the stretch for a few seconds, then return to the starting position. Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Engage your core muscles to support your lower back as you lean backward.
Avoid overextending your lower back; only lean back as far as comfortable without causing pain.
Breathe deeply throughout the exercise, inhaling as you prepare to stretch and exhaling as you lean back.
results.description: Elbow Back Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

results.name: Elbow Extension and Supination Pronation Forearm Stretch
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and your arms extended in front of you at hip level, palms open and over each other, with one hand crossing over the other.
Keep your palms crossed over each other and perform a wrist curl by bending your wrists upward.
Extend your wrists back down to the starting position.
Repeat the wrist curl and extension movements for the desired number of repetitions, then switch the position of your hands and repeat.
tips: Ensure your wrists and forearms do the majority of the movement, minimizing shoulder involvement.
Maintain straight arms and avoid bending your elbows during the stretch.
Perform the stretch with both hand positions to maintain muscle balance and flexibility.
results.description: Elbow Extension and Supination Pronation Forearm Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Biceps.

results.name: Elbow Flexor Stretch
instructions: Stand next to a wall with your feet shoulder-width apart, and extend your right arm out fully against the wall at shoulder height, palm facing the wall.
Rotate your torso away from the wall to increase the stretch in your arm.
Ensure your right arm is straight and press your palm firmly against the wall.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, feeling the stretch in your forearm and elbow flexors, then switch to the other arm.
tips: Ensure the stretch is felt in the forearm, elbow flexors, and chest muscles without causing pain.
Breathe deeply and steadily throughout the stretch, focusing on relaxing the muscles.
Perform the stretch on both arms to maintain muscle balance and flexibility.
results.description: Elbow Flexor Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the forearms (lower arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Biceps.

results.name: Elbows Back Stretch

Bring both hands behind you and place them on your lower back, fingers pointing downward.
Gently push your hips forward and lean your upper body backward, feeling a stretch in your chest and shoulders.
Hold the stretch for a few seconds, then return to the starting position. Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Engage your core muscles to support your lower back as you lean backward.
Avoid overextending your lower back; only lean back as far as comfortable without causing pain.
Breathe deeply throughout the exercise, inhaling as you prepare to stretch and exhaling as you lean back.
results.description: Elbows Back Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.
